A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the DiscoGP research, despite the changed title and sheaf terminology. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original GPT-2 circuit-discovery experiments, baseline comparisons, representation similarities, circuit overlaps, and attention-head analyses.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix D report original sheaf-discovery comparisons, mean-ablation and composition experiments, and relation-specific PARAREL training and test results.

M1.justification: The binary masks, straight-through estimator, and fidelity/completeness/sparsity objective are retained. V2 adds mask-union composition and a mean-ablation variant that replaces masked residual terms with reference averages. Weight-level granularity, split-QKV handling, and post-hoc graph pruning already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use English BLiMP, IOI, and the same 12 PARAREL relations. The determiner–noun variants tabulated explicitly in v2 already appear in v1's Table 4 and Section 6. The new composition and mean-ablation analyses reuse these tasks rather than introduce new data or task families.

E2.justification: V2 adds EAP throughout the benchmark comparisons and removes HISP. V1's SP corresponds to v2's weight-pruning baseline. V2 Appendix C explicitly identifies the cited edge-pruning method as equivalent to its edge-only setting, so that citation change is not an additional comparator.

E3.justification: V1 reports PARAREL test accuracy, whereas v2 Table 2 explicitly summarizes training accuracy and Appendix D separately reports training and test performance. V2 also introduces IOI mean-ablation and paired-mask composition protocols, and stops reporting node density. These changes prevent treating the headline PARAREL scores as a same-setting performance comparison.

E4.justification: V2 adds sheaf-composition experiments (Table 5) and a mean-ablation comparison (Table 3), while removing v1's sparsity–accuracy sweep and IOI head-distribution and layerwise-ablation analyses (Figures 3–5). Representation similarity, task overlap, and factual-recall analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5 first specifies five runs per experiment and reporting their average performance. V1 gives no run count. Neither reports confidence intervals or dispersion, and the new disclosure does not establish that the number of runs increased.

E6.justification: V2 replaces aggregate BLiMP reporting with six paradigm-level comparisons and adds EAP, composition, mean-ablation, and relation-specific PARAREL results. In the retained IOI comparison, weight-pruning complement accuracy changes from 50.0% to 57.5%, and edge-pruning complement accuracy from 57.5% to 49.9%. V1's 98.5% OQA test score and v2's 93.1% training average are not directly comparable.

T1.justification: V2 Equations 1–2 explicitly include current-block attention outputs in the MLP input, whereas v1 Section 2.1's expression for the MLP input sums only earlier-layer attention outputs. This is a limited correction to the residual-stream mathematics. The masking and loss equations remain essentially equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds reformulating circuit discovery through stricter faithfulness and completeness. V2 positions self-contained sheaf discovery as distinct from other circuit notions and foregrounds neuron-level granularity and modular composition. Its abstract also introduces the quantified claim of retaining 93–100% performance with 1–7% of weights and connections.

C2.justification: V2 adds a modularity interpretation of composition, explains PARAREL train–test gaps through dispersed factual knowledge, and explicitly acknowledges GPT-2 and English-only limitations. It distinguishes sheaf discovery from identifying influential components and questions greedy search. V1's specific diagnosis of missing lower-layer heads and MLPs in canonical IOI circuits is removed.

D1.justification: V2 reports available code/results, supplies baseline implementation URLs, and newly specifies reverse-BFS pruning and filtering PARAREL to model-correct examples. Conversely, v1's IOI sample count, checkpoint-selection rule, embedding-mask exclusions, and corrupted-input construction recipes disappear. Split-QKV and post-hoc pruning descriptions are largely relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the survey of circuit definitions, weight-pruning foundations, and recent discovery methods, including Syed et al., Bhaskar et al., and Mondorf et al. It repositions the contribution around distinct sheaves and composition in pretrained models, rather than principally correcting earlier circuit-discovery objectives.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the formulation and experimental narrative are rewritten around sheaves and functional fidelity. Implementation and baseline material move into dedicated appendices, analyses become three numbered findings, and a limitations section is added.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview, adds a multi-panel pruning illustration, restructures the main results table, and adds composition, mean-ablation, and detailed PARAREL tables. Three analytical figures disappear. The QKV diagram moves to the appendix, while the factual-recall plot is retained with corrected left/right caption descriptions.

improvement.justification: EAP comparisons, mean-ablation controls, five-run reporting, and detailed PARAREL train/test results strengthen parts of v2. However, the sparsity–accuracy sweep and useful replication details are removed. The abstract's 93–100% performance claim also fails to reflect PARAREL test accuracies of 57.7–95.6% in Tables 11–12; Table 2 instead summarizes training accuracy. These gains in evidence and transparency coexist with weaker support and qualification of central claims, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
